how tread MM bots work

as much as I love @tread_fi and fully recommend it, remember that it is not risk free

I've been farming the 10k XP @paradex (which has 0.2bps fees) competition and idk if I'll be net profitable with:

the paradex xp I get from MMing + from the competition (if I get lucky and win the raffle) + the tread points

paradex xp is currently selling at $0.2 OTC (which is far below $1B FDV, so I think there's a good chance it TGEs higher) and I expect to get ~4k XP for this volume, leaving me with >$800 if I don't win the raffle

what were my mistakes?

1) I used a 50x leverage bot with <100% of the recommended inventory (@davidyjeong has since patched this, you can thank me stepping into this abyss so that you don't have to) and I got my account liq'd for $900 on a random 2% wick

2) I ran a long bias bot on BTC and lost 1k to pnl because price started at $95.5k and ended at $93.6k (NB: david said that the chop here would've caused a neutral bias to wind up with -$700-800 pnl too)

3) I ran a short bias bot on SOL and lost 2k to pnl because price rose from $132 to $142

4) I ran a bot with a target of >$1M volume within a few hours and ended up being 90% of the XRP market

5) I ran a BTC short bot overnight, actually made $200, but it turned out that paradex do maintenance with no warning, the tread bot paused, didn't restart and left me holding a short from the pico bottom at $89.5k (I eventually managed to close this at a slight profit)

lessons:

1) use shorter bots and monitor them periodically so that you can nip funny business in the bud

2) always make sure your inventory is at least 10% more than the recommended inventory

3) accept that neutral bias will generally result in a -ve pnl and avoid using long/short bias unless you are a profitable trader and very sure of selecting the correct bias

it can be very profitable (I have hit a couple of profitable bots, albeit using much less vol than my unprofitable ones, rip), but nothing hits you in the gut like waking up to a -2k pnl

a 10x short bias on an mm bot is as risky, if not riskier, than opening a 10x short

imo it's actually much harder to trade profitably with a biased bot than it is on a normal trade

the biased bot works by front-loading the bias into the 1st half of the trade before closing it out in the 2nd half

eg/ if you set a short bias, like in the above SOL trade, the bot will place more sell limits than buy limits until halfway through (the min of the exposure parabola) and then vice versa after

the bot will try to following the blue exposure line, but it can visit the orange boundaries and is more likely to do so if you use higher aggressiveness (less time)

if the exposure crosses one of these orange lines, one side of the limits will pause until exposure reenters the band

so, why is this harder than normal trading?

i) the bot is constantly opening and closing trades, so you don't leave much time for the trade to start going your way; you are just betting that it will make more profitable mini-trades than unprofitable ones

ii) you aren't necessarily just betting that end price > start price for a long bias

you are betting either:

> price goes up only the whole time (this is the best case because it has the most buying low and selling high)

> price goes down only for the 1st half and then up only in the 2nd half

> price goes sideways in the 1st half and then up only in the 2nd

if you get the inverse of any of the 3 cases above, you lose (bigly)

if price goes sideways the whole time, theoretically, you'll be ~breakeven

this rather unintuitive (at least for me) and is not how we're used to approaching trades, so it takes a lot of experimenting (and losing money) to get the hang of (I evidently still haven't)

4) don't use more than 10x lev to avoid getting liq'd on wicks

NB: pnl is purely a function of volume; lev doesn't affect pnl risk, only liq risk

5) don't leave a bot overnight

6) maybe try out the delta neutral bot (I haven't used it much) because it might be cheaper, albeit less capital efficient

New OI / BBO dashboard just dropped on @tread_fi

At https://t.co/UH8qfLhxRk

After analyzing it, I realized it answers the most important MM question:

“Which markets should I even be market-making?”

Here’s what I understood from it and how you can use it to your advantage.

1)
First, what is OI (Open Interest)?

OI = total open positions in a market.
High OI = real traders, real positions, real flow.

Low OI = thin market → inventory traps.

—

2/
What is BBO (Best Bid / Offer)?

BBO = tightness of the order book.
Tight BBO = easy fills, stable execution.
Wide / jumpy BBO = you get clipped.

MM bots live and die by BBO stability.

⸻

3/
Now the important part
OI / BBO ratio

This ratio tells you:

How much real positioning exists relative to how efficient the order book is

In simple terms:
•High OI
•Tight spreads
= MM-friendly market

⸻

4/
Why OI alone is NOT enough 

A market can have high OI but:
•Wide spreads
•Violent price jumps
•Poor execution

That’s where BBO saves you.

⸻

5/
Why BBO alone is NOT enough

A market can have tight spreads but:
•No real traders
•No organic flow

Your bot becomes the market → dangerous.

⸻

6/
OI / BBO ratio combines both.

It answers one question:

“Will my MM bot be absorbed by the market or fight it?”

Absorbed = good
Fighting = bad

⸻

7/
How this helps pick profitable MM pairs 👇

 High OI / BBO ratio means:
•Strong two-sided flow
•Frequent fills
•Lower inventory risk
•Sustainable MM sessions

Perfect for volume + steady PnL.

⸻

8/
But here’s the trap 
High OI / BBO on LOW volume is misleading

Why?
•Ratio can look great
•But real trades are missing
•Liquidity disappears fast
•One move nukes your inventory

⸻

9/
Always cross-check with 24h volume.

Rule of thumb:
•High ratio + high volume = 🔥
•High ratio + low volume = ⚠️ fake comfort
•Low ratio + high volume = chop & danger

⸻

10/
So what should you actually choose?

The sweet spot:
•OI/BBO above market average
•Consistent 24h volume
•Ranging price behavior

⸻

11/

Attached image  is the current OI / BBO snapshot.

You’ll notice many pairs with very high ratios but low 24h volume  I skip these.
They’re usually unsustainable, caused by temporary order-book imbalances.

Refresh after a few minutes and most of them disappear.

What I look for instead:
•High OI/BBO
•High, consistent volume

That’s where MM bots get absorbed and execution stays clean.

From this snapshot, LITUSD, PAX, and EUR stand out.

High ratio without volume = noise.
High ratio + volume = opportunity.

12/
Final thought:

Most MM losses don’t come from bad bot settings.
They come from choosing the wrong market.

OI / BBO ratio fixes that

how @tread_fi mm bot actually works

and how to launch it safe for your balance

market making with tread is not free yield
you're basically renting a very fast trader that:

- posts both bids and asks around the mid
- tries to keep your net exposure inside a controlled band instead of letting you drift into a huge directional bet
- farm tread points

in the video below i walk through the clicks:

> step one - pick the market and leverage

if you farm @tradexyz or @ventuals be careful, those markets completely static on weekends and bot most likely will stop.

there's no problems with majors though (btc, eth, hype, etc.)

for less risk choose leverage below 10x

> step two - fund and size the bot

before you touch settings, make sure your inventory is at least a bit higher than the recommended inventory size (think +10-20% buffer)

otherwise you have a risk of liquidations

recommended inventory depends on the budget, bias and mode

you should be ok with that whole amount being actively traded. this is not a tiny test order, this is your working capital for the bot

> step three - choose bias type

neutral mm
goal: max volume with min price impact 
not profit and no loss, you're just burning dex fees in range of your budget 

use this if you don't have a strong view on direction

long / short skew
goal: combine mm with a directional opinion
bot front-loads your bias in the first half of the run and unwinds later

path matters: you need price behavior to roughly match your bias path (best case is up/down only), not just end higher/lower

even if you bet on right direction positive pnl is not guaranteed, you should test with small amount at first to understand algos.

> step four - execution mode

aggressive
- tighter around mid, more fills, faster volume
- better for mega-liquid markets where you just want to get done and reduce exposure quickly

normal
- good default for most large pairs
- balances between getting hit and not chasing every move

passive
- behave closer to a grid: slower, wider
- potentially higher returns over longer periods but you need patience and monitoring

> step five - run and monitor

once the bot is live, watch:
-  pnl and executed notional (are you bleeding per notional traded?)
- participation rate (if you're 80–90% of the market, you're basically trading against yourself)

if something looks off, pause early. make sure all positions are closed and orders are canceled.

TLDR;
inventory is your work balance, it will be used to open positions 

keep inventory buffer at least at 10%, running with less than recommended inventory is how you get forced into bad fills or even liquidations on a weird move. a bit more inventory = more room for the bot to rebalance without panicking.

bias is harder than it looks, with a skewed bot you're not just betting end price > start price, you're betting on the path

monitor often, there are a lot of unpredicted maintenances happens on dexes side

using @tread_fi delta-neutral bot to farm funding

if you already farm funding on perps, you don't need to manually open positions every time.

tread delta-neutral (DN) bot does it safely for you and keeps you close to flat on price

simple example

you see a clean funding spread on $ZEC
long on paradex, short on hyperliquid = ~250% apr on any reasonable size

the DN bot lets you open that pair as a single trade using a TWAP execution instead of market slamming both sides.

> how it works in practice:

you choose a long leg
exchange + pair where you want to be long

you choose a short leg
exchange + pair where you want to be short 

you set notional
this is total size, the bot automatically splits 50/50 between long and short

you pick leverage
only changes margin usage and liq risk, not pnl per dollar of funding. keep it conservative so random wicks or small imbalances don't ruin the trade

you pick mode
aggressive = fast open, more impact
normal = balanced default
passive = slow, less impact 

all of them use TWAP so you don't get filled in one ugly candle

> what to monitor

net sided funding rate

this is the combined funding from both legs after sign adjustments, could be a bit less than real rate (aster funding is not tracked)

you want it clearly positive after you mentally subtract trading fees (2bps builder + maker fees on venues)

status
opening = bot is still building both legs
open = position is live, now you just monitor funding and exposure
wind down = when you're done, you press wind down and it twaps out of both legs for you

> things people forget
funding changes every 8h, the spread you see now is not guaranteed forever

both legs pay fees, so tiny spreads get eaten by costs

delta-neutral still has execution + imbalance risk if you oversize or ignore exposure

used correctly, the DN bot turns "open two legs, check size, adjust, close both" into one structured action

you focus on finding clean, sustainable funding spreads, the bot focuses on getting you in and out without turning a funding arb into a hidden directional bet.

The Problem With Fixed Fee Builder Codes

Builder codes enable applications like wallets (@phantom) and trading interfaces (@tread_fi) to route user transactions through perpetual protocols (@HyperliquidX) while earning a share of the fees. The fee structure here really matters. Fixed minimums create barriers, while revenue sharing unlocks experimentation.

If a customer has ten dollars to spend on transaction fees. Under a traditional fixed-cost model, if the underlying protocol charges five dollars, only five dollars remain for the builder layer. This creates an inherent zero-sum competition: the protocol and builder are fighting over the same limited pie, each trying to extract maximum value from a fixed budget.

They’re simultaneously partners and competitors, creating a fundamental tension that stifles innovation. When there’s a hard line in the sand – “you must pay three basis points” – builders face an immovable hurdle that constrains their ability to experiment, optimize, and ultimately deliver value to end users.

The Revenue Sharing Alternative

Instead of competing for a fixed pie, the protocol takes a percentage of whatever the builder earns. If the builder can only capture one basis point from the customer, they pay the protocol some percentage of that one basis point. If they find innovative ways to capture ten basis points, the protocol benefits proportionally from that success, and the builders benefit even more from the value they create for themselves and the protocol. It’s advantageous for builders because they can experiment and discover new ways to frame the pie, while the protocol earns more revenue as it becomes home to the best founders. 

Builders, in turn, gain the freedom to experiment aggressively with pricing models, user experiences, and value propositions without worrying about clearing a mandatory cost hurdle. Zero fee builder codes enables this type of revenue share model and also unlocks a unique distribution mechanism for the perp DEX: trading venues can credibly market themselves as the cheapest venue while simultaneously expanding their margins. This increases distribution into things like wallets. Assuming liquidity is the same, do you think Phantom would use a builder code that has revenue share or one that has mandatory hurdles? 

Rather than fighting over how to divide ten dollars, the focus shifts to growing that ten dollars into twenty dollars. Builders closest to the customer have the best visibility into what users value and what they’re willing to pay for (look at @BasedAppHQ).

Whether it’s an app store, Roblox’s creator economy, or other successful marketplace models, the winning formula consistently involves revenue sharing rather than fixed listing fees. Creators can start small, test ideas, and scale what works, all while the platform benefits proportionally from successful experiments.

The Path Forward

By aligning incentives between protocols and builders, revenue sharing creates the conditions for genuine experimentation, rapid iteration, and ultimately, the kind of thinking that expands entire markets. I expect, over time, more teams utilizing builder codes will prefer zero fee builder codes.

Treadtools es un dashboard en tiempo real creado por el propio equipo de Tread para analizar mercados de perpetuals disponibles en su plataforma.

👉 ayudarte a elegir los pares óptimos para lanzar bots de Market Maker en modo Grid, reduciendo PnL rojo y mejorando fills mientras generas volumen.

•50% estabilidad de precio
•25% OI/BBO (open interest vs liquidez top-of-book)
•25% volumen relativo

•Stability alta = precio calmado
•Status: solo Calm o Steady
•OI/BBO alto = menos competencia MM
•Volume suficiente para fills reales

Este combo marca la diferencia entre un bot que dura y uno que salta el SL en minutos.

Grid vs RGrid is live on @tread_fi MM bots. 
Here’s the breakdown 👇

Try the new mode here: https://t.co/pqXnovxPrx

📈 Best market
• Grid: sideways
• RGrid: trending + volatile

🧠 Core logic
• Grid: buy low → sell high
• RGrid: buy high → sell low

💰 Profit mechanism
• Grid: captures spread
• RGrid: captures big swings

💧 Liquidity role
• Grid: mostly maker
• RGrid: mostly taker

🎯 Take-profit / reset
• Grid: hard stop, usually ~±0.5% from last fill
• RGrid: resets / takes profit when price drifts X% from reference

⚠️ Risks
• Grid: strong trend = fewer fills, stagnation, possible bag-holding
• RGrid: small residual exposure, small negative PnL can happen on flips

✅ Rule of thumb
Sideways → Grid
Strong trend → RGrid

Hot take, but with the 90% fee cuts on HIP 3, I think the real winners are not the farmers. 

The real winner is @tread_fi 

Yesterday, @hyperliquidX shipped Growth Mode in the latest network update. Since then, @tradexyz and @felixprotocol have already enabled it on their markets. This lets you enjoy a 90% discount on both maker and taker fees on eligible assets.

This is a big step toward bringing more players into the equity markets. High fees were a real pain point I talked about a while ago, so seeing this addressed is very positive.

One detail that many people miss is that with the discounted fees, the weight of the volume you generate on these markets is also reduced by 90%. So if you are farming volume on HIP 3 markets for a potential airdrop ($ for potentially more $), you should factor that into your strategy.

If you push $100k of volume, only $10k of that now counts toward your weighted volume. To get the same score as $100k before, you now need $1M.

Now to my hot take. I think the biggest winner from this new wave of volume and market making is @tread_fi.

With a 90% fee discount, in the worst case you pay 0.009% on taker fees and 0.003% on maker fees. On top of that you still pay the builder fee, in this case 0.02%, which on its own is more than 2x the taker fee and around 6x the maker fee.

Quick example with $100k of volume:
Pure taker:
• Hyperliquid fee at 0.009% = 9 dollars
• Builder fee at 0.02% = 20 dollars
• Total = 29 dollars, and the builder fee is about 70% of what you pay

Pure maker:
• Hyperliquid fee at 0.003% = 3 dollars
• Builder fee at 0.02% = 20 dollars
• Total = 23 dollars, and the builder fee is almost 90% of what you pay

So the builder fee is now the dominant cost.

On top of that, the bots they provide are in my view losing money over time. Even if they are presented as delta neutral, you are very likely to bleed. If they had a model that was reliably profitable, there would be no reason to offer it to the public.

That said, credit where it is due. They found a market in eager farmers and built something that sells. You can see they are consistently in the top 3 to 5 by revenue generated from HIP 3 markets, so kudos to them.

It is the same basic pattern as during the gold rush, where the real money was made by companies selling shovels rather than by most people digging for gold. More recently you see the same thing with course sellers. Do not hate the player, hate the game.

how the @tread_fi  MM bot works (running now with $5M target notional on @paradex )

1. what it does
+MM bot runs a simple loop: 
+places a buy order slightly below market
+places a sell order slightly above market
+when either side fills, it instantly replaces both orders
+as price moves, it shifts the orders so they always sit around the current price
+builder fee of 0.02% of notional

2. how it manages risk
+as fills come in, the bot keeps the position balanced:
+too many buys? bot posts more sells, and vice versa
+this prevents you from accidentally drifting into a giant long or short exposure

3. how size is deployed
+ notional($5M in my case) is split across many small trades
+TWAP sends these small trades in slowly so you don’t move the market or leak size

4. benefits
+automate my farming and don't let capital sit idle
+earn the spread & stay market neutral
+more capital efficient than the DN bot which needs more margin in your wallet

¿Qué debemos buscar? La Lógica del OI/BBO 🧠

Muchos miran solo el volumen, pero eso es un error. Para encontrar actividad real y segura, debemos calcular el ratio entre dos factores:

Open Interest (OI): Es el interés abierto. Cuanto más alto, más dinero y posiciones hay involucradas en ese mercado. Significa liquidez real.

Best Bid/Offer (BBO): La calidad de la mejor oferta en el libro de órdenes.

💡 La Estrategia:Busquen en la tabla el par que tenga el Mayor Ratio OI/BBO combinado con un volumen alto. Esto nos indica un mercado sano donde nuestro bot puede operar fluidamente sin ser "atropellado".

katexbt가 이 흐름을 2026년의 0→1 메타라고 부른 이유는 수익률보다 접근성이 바뀌었다는 점이 더 크다고 느끼기 때문이라고 느껴집니다.

- 기관의 기술이 도구가 된다
MM은 본질적으로 양방향 호가를 깔고 스프레드로 수익을 내는 행위인데 문제는 자동화, 리스크 관리, 실행 품질이 전부 시스템 싸움이라 리테일이 접근하기 어려웠다는 점이 있습니다.

TreadFi는 이걸 설정 가능한 봇이라는 형태로 풀어냈습니다.
그 결과 리테일은 직접 마켓메이킹 비즈니스를 운영한다기보다 초기 제품을 사용하며 거래량과 포인트를 함께 쌓는 플레이어가 됬죠.

- Perp DEX 시즌과의 결합
2025년의 perpdex 경쟁은 거래량과 포인트를 중심으로 설계됐으며 TreadFi는 여러 거래소에서 반쯤 자동으로 볼륨을 만든다는 욕구와 정확히 맞물립니다.

그래서 이 툴의 핵심 가치는 돈을 프린트하는 기계라기보다는 볼륨 생산을 표준화하는 인프라가 된다는 데 있다고 봅니다.

- 설정 싸움, 그리고 리스크 싸움
katexbt 의 레시피는 전반적으로 보수적이라고 합니다.
낮은 레버리지, 더 많은 자기자본, 그리드 기반 운영, 스프레드는 시장에 맞춰 조정, 손절은 변동성에 맞게 설정하는거죠.

여기서 중요한 건 볼륨만 만들면 된다 는 환상에 빠지지 않는 것이 중요합니다. MM은 결국 재고를 들고 가는 게임이고 시장이 급격히 움직이면 스프레드 수익보다 손실이 더 커질 수도 있습니다.

여기까지가 원래 기존의 해당글의 관련된 내용이며 해당내용은 거래의 노동 및 방법을 새롭게 변화하는 과정처럼 보였는데 해당글과관련해서 여러문의가 있었는지 추가내용을 달아주었는데 해당내용도 마저 정리해드릴게요.

- 추가내용( 이건 ‘돈 버는 기계’가 아니다 )
몇 번의 안정적인 PnL 스크린샷 때문에 사람들이 이걸 꾸준히 돈 버는 봇으로 오해할 수 있다는 점이었어요.

Tried the @tread_fi  mm and delta-neutral bots for the first time a couple days ago, mainly on @pacifica_fi.

Initial thoughts below 

TLDR: MM bot is currently costly, but delta neutral bot is probably the best way to run neutral strats now

Market Maker bot: 
PnL was negative all 15/15 runs (most users reporting similar)

When run with neutral bias, the bot places simultaneous buy/sells around the cmp, so I naively expected it would be sometimes +, sometimes -, but this wasn't the case. 

I'm not sure if this is some toxic flow thing, or just a natural result of the how the bot's placing orders. But between fees and PnL, it ends up costing ~ $10 per $15k volume (which isn't great). 

Breakdown:

-Pacifica maker fee: 0.015%

-Treadfi builder fee: 0.02% (higher than the underlying perpdex, which is a little surprising)

-PnL: consistently about the same as combined fees, ~0.035%

I also tried with a long directional bias. This frontloads the buys and backloads the sells, so you should be buying low/selling high if the price is moving up (which it was)

This improved PnL somewhat, but not enough to flip it positive:

Delta-neutral bot: much better experience

There are usually a couple issues when doing this manually:
1. have to place market orders and pay taker fees
2. price discrepancy means you often end up net negative

However, trading @pacifica_fi against @HyperliquidX , I found: 
1. bot works by placing incremental limit orders on both sides (so no market orders)

although @tread_fi fees eat most of the maker-taker fee difference, you're earning points in exchange

2. close match between the +pnl on one side and -pnl on the other

All in all, a cheaper, more reliable, and less time consuming way to delta neutral.

FYI: Pure volume is not a cost-effective way to earn @pacifica_fi  points. But you can use delta neutral to make "good" trades on the pacifica side with much larger volume than you normally would.

Here is simple guide explaining its functionality and usefulness 

The TreadFi delta-neutral bot is designed to automate funding-rate farming, a strategy where you earn money from the difference in funding payments between exchanges.

Normally, doing this manually is tedious: you have to open a long position on one exchange, open an equal-sized short on another, make sure both sides are the same size, avoid slippage, adjust your position when the market moves, and later close both legs without accidentally taking on price exposure.

You start by picking your long exchange and pair, then your short exchange and pair. You enter one total notional value, and the bot automatically splits it 50/50 between long and short. It then opens both legs using TWAP, which means it spreads your order out over time in small pieces to avoid bad fills, spikes, or expensive candles

Once the position is live, the bot keeps you close to delta-neutral, meaning your long and short stay balanced so you don’t end up with an accidental directional bet.

 You just keep an eye on the “net funding rate,” which is how much funding you’re earning after fees. When the bot says the position is “open,” it’s already running; when you’re done, you hit “wind down,” and it exits both sides the same smooth way. 

This setup helps reduce mistakes, keeps your price exposure close to zero, and turns a normally annoying two-leg process into one simple action—so you can focus on finding good funding spreads instead of manually trading every time.

The TreadFi bot does all of this work for you.
